title: slice-mapper-latency-profiles-and-benchmark-orchestration-per-route-model-region
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an end-to-end harness and dashboard surface that maps p95/p99 latency profiles across the triad of route, model, and region and surfaces regressions automatically. This ticket covers orchestration, slice definition, synthetic workload generation, baseline computation, alerting hooks, and dashboard panels.

Background: Current telemetry is fragmented by route or model but lacks a compact mapping that teams can use to triage regressions across region/model/route intersections. Our objective is to provide: (1) deterministic benchmark runs for tokens/sec and latency tail quantiles, (2) slice-level baselines and historical context, and (3) automated regression detection that creates Linear tickets and Slack alerts when thresholds diverge.

Scope and deliverables:
- A slice-mapper component that materializes all active slices (route x model x region) and a lightweight rule engine to prioritize top N slices by traffic and recent variance.
- Load runner scenarios that simulate token emission distributions and KV-cache priming states (cold/warm/hot). Each scenario produces tokens/sec and runtime p95/p99 metrics.
- Orchestration job in CI that runs nightly systemic benches and on-demand runs for releases or model rollouts. Results get persisted to the telemetry store with per-run metadata (runner-config, seed, priming-state).
- Regression detector that compares the latest run against a rolling baseline (median-of-last-10 or weighted-EXP) and flags statistically significant uplifts in p95/p99 and large drops in tokens/sec. Detector should support both absolute thresholds and relative delta %.
- Dashboard panels in Console: a matrix view with rows=routes, cols=models, small-multiples by region. Drill-in view shows time series, distribution violin, and recent runs with metadata and link to the failing run artifact.
- Alerting workflow: on detection create a draft Linear ticket with prefilled evidence (diff graphs, top affected slices) and post an annotated message to #latency-alerts. Provide a manual acknowledge/close flow from the dashboard.

Constraints & trade-offs considered:
- Accuracy vs cost: Nightly full-grid runs are expensive; we will default to a top-N sampling strategy plus deterministic smoke runs for the remaining slices.
- Synthetic realism vs reproducibility: Use parameterized pseudo-random seeds for reproducible runs; retain a smaller set of stochastic scenarios for fuzz coverage.
- Storage: Persist summarized distributions (histogram buckets + sketches) rather than raw traces to keep retention affordable.

Implementation notes / tasks:
1) Slice mapper service (engine) + API (ENG-17234-1) - enumerates slices, exposes top-N selection and filters.
2) Load runner extension (ENG-17234-2) - new runner flags for token emission profiles, KV cache priming.
3) Baseline service (ENG-17234-3) - rolling baseline computation and candidate selection logic.
4) Regression detector (ENG-17234-4) - statistical tests and significance thresholds; should support bootstrap and nonparametric approaches.
5) Dashboard panels (ENG-17234-5) - matrix and drill-down, run artifact links, ticket/alert button.
6) CI integration and nightly job (ENG-17234-6) - pipeline + storage hooks.
7) Runbook and playbook (ENG-17234-7) - triage steps and ownership.

Progress so far:
- Initial slice-mapper prototype completed and validated against production route list (PR #12345).
- Load runner hooks merged into the forked runner; added KV-priming flag and token-distribution profiles (PR #12358).
- Baseline sketching prototype (histogram + EWMA) is running in staging but needs calibration windows.

Open questions:
- Default sampling policy: fixed top-200 slices by weighted traffic or dynamic percentile-based? Proposal: start with top-200 and revisit after 2 weeks of telemetry.
- Regression detection threshold: use 95% confidence via bootstrap or a delta > 15% p95? Action: pair with Data Science for validation.

Dependencies: nightly-run infra (ENG-30777) for runners, telemetry-warehouse retention change (ENG-19111) to keep 90 days of synthesized histograms, and alerting integration (ENG-20012).

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field below.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Slice-mapper enumerates and exposes all active route:model:region slices and a top-N selection API.
2) Load runner produces reproducible p95/p99 and tokens/sec metrics for cold/warm/hot priming states; sample artifacts stored for each run.
3) Nightly orchestration persists summarized histograms and sketch artifacts for at least 90 days.
4) Regression detector flags significant p95/p99 regressions and creates a draft Linear ticket with evidence.
5) Dashboard matrix surfaces per-slice p95/p99 and tokens/sec, supports region filters and drill-down to run artifacts.
6) On-chart alert creation posts to #latency-alerts with links and creates the draft ticket.
7) Documentation and runbook published in Confluence and linked from the dashboard.
notes:
Review feedback from PM: prefer conservative defaults for alert noise reduction; include an opt-out toggle per route. Design request: compact matrix should support colorblind-accessible palettes. Engineering note: prioritize low-overhead runners for nightly grid.

Next steps: schedule pairing with Data Science for statistical thresholding (week of 2026-03-15). Prepare a shortlist of top-200 slices and run a 3-day smoke run to calibrate baseline windows.
review_feedback: PM (Lena Morales): prefer default top-N policy and a throttle to reduce noise
Design (Marco Ruiz): matrix needs a compact glyph that encodes p95/p99 and tokens/sec simultaneously
